To anyone interested, the iOS app is still in active development. There have been many changes to iOS, and I decided about a month ago to start re-writing the app in Swift instead of the existing code that I had in Objective-C.

I really do not like to put out sub-par products, so I'm going to do this the correct way and not push anything out to quickly, which is why I am not advertising this in any sub verses. It takes quite a bit of additional effort to make an efficient and performant app - someone could throw together an HTML5/Angular/React app more quickly, but that road is usually not going to make an end user happy.

As far as the current status goes, I am finishing up writing the api layer (with Alamofire), and I hope to get some of the essential UI in place by the end of July/Aug. I have a full time job, so this has to fit in when time allows.
